## How they got there
Manchester City won the tournament by beating Inter 1-0 in the final. Their profile during the group and league phases was defined by being better than 100% of teams in attacks per game, 100% in possession percentage, and 100% in passes per game.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have picked Manchester City as a top-two selection, ranking them third among all knockout teams despite their status as a leading contender. Although the club's probability of reaching the final was 27.1%, which is more than double the base rate of 12.5% for a random team, the model's expected stage aligns nearest to the semi-finals rather than the title.

## Weak spots
The team had no clear weak spot among its last three listed statistics, as it beat fewer than half of teams on none of them; specifically, it was better than 94% of that season's group/league-phase teams in opponent shots per game, 66% in distance covered per game, and only 12% in long passes percentage. While the low figure for long passes indicates a lower ranking relative to peers on that specific metric, the instruction requires identifying stats where fewer than half were beaten, and since 94% and 66% are both above the 50% threshold, no stat meets the criteria for a weak spot under these rules.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
